page: Amazon Web Services m5.16xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8175M processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 3.1 GHz. The configuration provides 64 virtual CPUs mapped to 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It includes 256.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, translating to 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it features a baseline network bandwidth of 20 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear division between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core processing speeds, evaluated via stress-ng and Geekbench, fall into the lower tier. However, multi-core performance scales to average levels, as demonstrated by stress-ng multi-core and Passmark CPU scores. Memory performance is a notable highlight, with large-block read-only memory bandwidth reaching a strong 192.72 GB/sec, while small-block reads and large-block writes remain average.

Given its balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the m5.16xlarge is suited for multi-threaded general-purpose workloads, including static web serving, Redis database operations, and software compilation, which all perform at average levels. It is less optimal for single-threaded tasks or heavy LLM text generation, where benchmark results are weak. The absence of local storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which should be factored into the overall resource density and architectural planning.
